description.en: A source-verified MiniMax H3 music video prompt with attached video evidence from @ou_zhen599.
description.zh: 由原作者公开 X 帖提供并已核验视频结果的 MiniMax H3音乐视频提示词。

prompt:
For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] A 15-second, 16:9, cinematic photoreal image-to-video sequence based on <Picture 1>, unfolding entirely inside the same misty reed field and forest-edge zone at dawn. Keep the space, weather, time, and lighting fully continuous: warm golden backlight from high behind her, thin fog through wet reeds, damp mud, dew, and shallow reflective moisture. No scene change, no buildings, no vehicles, no extra people, no environmental drift. Preserve the same elite adult female tactical shooter throughout: black high ponytail, sunglasses, fitted black combat top, tactical vest, waist rig, and the same rifle. Identity, face, proportions, hairstyle, outfit, gear, and weapon remain stable. She never stops; the action is one continuous chain: advancing, tightening steps, parting reeds, raising the rifle, lowering into a half-crouch, scanning, changing muzzle direction, and pressing the earpiece to report. Her sensuality comes only from danger, control, breath, and precision, never posing. The camera has a pseudo-one-take quality with hidden transitions only through reeds wiping the lens, the rifle crossing frame, or her body occluding view. [Shot 2] At 00:00.000-00:02.400, the camera skims low over dew-heavy roots and wet mud, then rises into a medium-close right-rear tracking shot glued to her body. She advances while lifting the rifle from low carry to chest-high ready with the right hand, the left shoulder subtly bracing the sling. Her ponytail moves with soft weighted delay, small face-framing strands shift in the breeze, and the combat fabric forms tiny real wrinkles at shoulder, chest, waist, and inner arm. This opening is the dangerous close body study: neck, jawline, lip line, sunglasses edge, rifle, sling, and upper-body control in one moving frame. Her first emotional layer is quiet alertness: lips pressed into a thin clean line, jaw lightly tucked, breathing fine and steady, brows relaxed, head direction unwavering. [Shot 3] At 00:02.400, the camera becomes a low eye-level parallel tracking medium shot with reeds brushing the foreground. She never stops moving, but her footfalls become lighter and quieter. Her left hand parts the tall wet grass while the rifle muzzle enters the gap first, and her center of gravity lowers gradually. A tiny metallic impact sounds ahead and one patch of reeds moves unnaturally. Her second layer appears: the head tips slightly toward the sound, the brow center gathers by a trace, the gaze narrows from patrol scan into search focus, the nostrils open once and settle, the mouth corners pull inward slightly, and the breath shortens and thins. She murmurs in a low restrained tone: <d>[Chinese] Too quiet.</d> [Shot 4] At 00:05.000, the camera arcs to a front-right forty-five-degree angle, shifting between close and medium close while staying tied to her shoulder line and gun line. She lowers her body further and cuts sideways into a narrower gap in the reeds. The rifle stock seats toward the shoulder, the trigger finger stays outside the trigger, and the left hand continues parting denser grass while her footwork becomes lower, quieter, and more deliberate. Sling, waist attachments, and ponytail carry subtle delayed inertia. Under the opened reeds, a blood-stained tactical glove appears first, then a severed communications earpiece cable, then a dark wet stain at the roots. Her third emotional layer emerges: search range narrows sharply, lower lids tighten, outer eye line drops, jaw muscle firms, lip line thins, the throat gives one nearly invisible swallow, and the breath catches for a fraction. [Shot 5] At 00:07.600, the camera follows the rifle and her line of sight forward, lowering into a tight grass-gap close view. Her front foot checks briefly into the mud, but her body never freezes; she stays in a half-crouched forward-pressure posture, rifle pointed outward, left hand still moving reeds aside. Beneath the grass lies the upper half of a fallen teammate, partly turned onto one side, half the face buried into mud and wet vegetation, a clear shoulder identification patch visible, and a close-range gunshot wound at the side of the neck. Blood stays real and restrained: heavy damp staining into roots and mud, dark adhesive spread with real viscosity, not sprayed decoration. The earpiece wire trembles faintly in the breeze. Her fourth emotional layer appears: lips part by a fraction and close again, lower lids tighten, nostrils widen once, the gaze locks hard and briefly freezes, the brow center concentrates tighter, and cheek and jawline harden together. She breathes out one tiny line, almost caught in the throat: <d>[Chinese] No...</d> [Shot 6] At 00:10.000, the camera returns quickly to a near frontal three-quarter close shot, keeping her upper body, rifle, shoulder line, and misted background readable. She does not freeze. She immediately lifts her gaze left, then right, then forward, driving the muzzle with the same sequence while sinking lower into the grass. Her fifth emotional layer is shock compressed back into function: brows tighten but stay controlled, the eye opening widens only slightly, lower lids become fully tense, lips press shut, the jaw and masseter lock, and side-neck tendons rise. Fog parts under her motion and the muzzle, while the corpse’s earpiece wire continues its small movement in the background. [Shot 7] At 00:12.000, the same close-to-medium-close camera system continues with a subtle forward drift. One hand holds the rifle steady while the other quickly presses the earpiece. Her eyes continue changing observation points through the fog without ever looking at the camera. She remains in a low half-crouch, ready to explode into action. Her final emotional layer is professional report and threat-lock at once: the gaze turns colder and faster, the brow center tightens and stabilizes, the lip line stays hard and short, the nostrils mark each observation shift with tiny breath changes, and the neck and collarbone carry persistent micro-tension. She reports in Chinese, low, fast, and controlled: <d>[Chinese] 指挥部，芦苇区发现一名队员倒地。敌人还在附近，回话。</d> End on a suspended dangerous hold with her crouched in the reeds, rifle ready, eyes still searching into the mist, waiting for response. Do not cut to black.

overall_soundscape: The soundscape is led by environment: wet footsteps in mud, reeds brushing fabric and weapon, sling and gear taps, restrained breathing, distant forest wind, faint metallic contact, and the tiny friction of the earpiece wire. Emphasize close bodily motion in the opening, then reeds scraping against fabric and barrel, dew flicking off leaves, and quieter stepping as she tightens her patrol. Let <d>[Chinese] Too quiet.</d> sit almost inside the breath. Compress the discovery zone sonically with mud suction, grass drag, cable tremor, and the nearly swallowed <d>[Chinese] No...</d>, then preserve a low environmental bed under the final Chinese radio report so the words land without removing wind and reeds entirely.

non_diegetic_music: Use almost no music. If any score is present, keep it as an extremely low, slow pressure bed entering only in the middle-to-late section. It must never dominate footsteps, reeds, breathing, or the radio line. The ending should stay unresolved and tense rather than dramatic or emotional.
